knowledge:
- key_parameters: normalized.data=An expression matrix where genes are rows and experiments are columns, normalized such that gene expression values are distributed uniformly between -1 and 1 ;; query=A character vector of gene or probeset identifiers representing the query genes of interest ;; ngenes=The number of top-ranked genes to return in the main result ;; fun=A scoring function applied to the ranks of the query genes to determine how many experiments to include (defaults to median) ;; extra=A logical value; if TRUE, the output includes additional metrics such as fifty.percent.recall, experiments.included, experiments.excluded, s.g.i (biological significance), z.g.i (statistical significance), and contribution (experiment-wise contribution)
- alternatives: Alternative normalization can be performed by applying qnorm((normalized.data + 1)/2) to the output of gr.normalize to obtain a standard normal distribution instead of a uniform distribution. The original algorithm from Owen et al. (2003) is an alternative, but this package is preferred as it uses a more accurate incremental method instead of a grid approach and uses median instead of mean for robustness.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have a list of genes known to be functionally related (the query) and want to discover new, functionally related genes from microarray expression data, even in the presence of significant missing data.
- pitfalls: Running the algorithm on unnormalized expression data (always use gr.normalize first) ;; including query genes that are regulated differently from the rest of the query (use gr.cv to identify these; a very large rank indicates a query gene that may not belong) ;; expecting identical results to the original Owen et al. paper (results differ slightly due to the incremental experiment selection and the use of median instead of mean).

workflows.name: targeted_gene_recommendation
workflows.intent: Identify and rank genes coexpressed with a query set of genes in microarray data, with options for cross-validation and custom scoring.
input: geneData (microarray expression matrix with genes as rows and experiments as columns)
my.query (character vector of query gene/probeset IDs)
workflows.stages: 1. Normalize the expression matrix using gr.normalize (and optionally transform with qnorm). ;; 2. Perform targeted clustering and ranking using gr.main. ;; 3. Validate the query genes using leave-one-out cross-validation with gr.cv.
workflows.code:
library(geneRecommender)
data(geneData)
my.query <- c("31613_at", "31712_at", "31497_at")
normalized.data <- gr.normalize(geneData)
gr.main(normalized.data, my.query, ngenes = 10)
gr.cv(normalized.data, my.query)
normal.normalized.data <- qnorm((normalized.data + 1)/2)
gr.main(normal.normalized.data, my.query, ngenes = 10)
my.fun.1 <- function(input.vector){
  sum(input.vector^(1/2), na.rm = T)
}
gr.main(normalized.data, my.query, ngenes = 10, fun = my.fun.1)
gr.main(normalized.data, my.query, ngenes = 10, extra = T)
